newsitem.title: UK: UK shares open lower after BoE rate-hike call.
newsitem.headline: UK shares open lower after BoE rate-hike call.

text.p: UK shares opened lower on Tuesday, unnerved by a call for higher interest rates by Bank of England Governor Eddie George and apprehension ahead of a speech by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.

George's warning that there were "real dangers" in letting sterling strength delay a rate rise rekindled market speculation that interest rates could go up in early February and countered any positive impact for UK shares of another record Dow close.
By 0838 GMT the FTSE 100 index was 12.2 points lower at 4,181.8, while the March long gilt future was dowm 4/32 at 110-25/32. The Dow closed 10.7 points higher at 6,843.87.
Greenspan is scheduled to speak at a U.S. Senate Budget Committee hearing at 1500 GMT.
